DrWang.description: conversing about a patient consulting Dr. Wang about facial redness and itching likely caused by a new laundry detergent, leading to a diagnosis of contact dermatitis and a treatment plan involving discontinuing the detergent, using a gentle cleanser, and applying a mild topical steroid twice daily for up to 7 days. @ <persona> PatientB
chat: PatientB

Hi Dr. Wang, I’ve been having facial redness and itching for the past three days, and I was planning to come see you at the dermatology clinic today. I’m a bit worried it might be an allergy—could you please take a look?
DrWang
Thanks for coming in. Let’s take a look. Can you tell me if anything new triggered this—like skincare products, detergents, or foods? Also, is the redness and itching constant or does it come and go?
PatientB

I haven’t changed my skincare routine recently, but I did start using a new laundry detergent about four days ago—right before the symptoms started. The redness and itching have been pretty constant, especially around my cheeks and forehead, and it gets worse when I touch or rub my face.
DrWang

That timing with the new detergent is notable. I’ll examine your skin now. Based on what you’ve described, it sounds like contact dermatitis. I’ll likely recommend stopping the new detergent and using a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser. I may also prescribe a mild topical steroid to reduce inflammation and itching—nothing oral unless it worsens.
PatientB
Thank you, Dr. Wang. That makes sense—I’ll stop using the new detergent right away. Could you also let me know how often I should apply the topical steroid and for how long?
DrWang

Apply the topical steroid twice daily—morning and evening—for up to 7 days. If the redness or itching doesn’t improve within that time, or if it spreads or worsens, come back for a follow-up. Avoid scrubbing or using any other new products on your face in the meantime.
